paper.title: Physics-Informed Weakly Supervised Learning for Interatomic Potentials
paper.research_summary: We address this challenge by introducing a physics-informed, weakly supervised approach for training machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs). We introduce two novel loss functions, extrapolating the potential energy via a Taylor expansion and using the concept of conservative forces. Our approach improves the accuracy of MLIPs applied to training tasks with sparse training data sets and reduces the need for pre-training computationally demanding models with large data sets.

task.objective: to learn an MLIP, which can accurately predict the potential energy and atomistic forces for an atomic system exposed to local perturbations
constraints: limited sizes of available data sets
high computational cost of ab initio or first-principles approaches
output_goal: accurate prediction of potential energy and atomistic forces

evidence.text: We address this challenge by introducing a physics-informed, weakly supervised approach for training machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs).
Our method is designed to learn an MLIP, which can accurately predict the potential energy and atomistic forces for an atomic system exposed to local perturbations.

evidence.text: They require the generation of training data sets that sufficiently cover configurational (atom positions) and compositional (atom types) spaces using, e.g., molecular dynamics (MD) simulations based on ab initio or first-principles approaches.

stages.stage_goal: to assess the robustness during MD simulations of the MLIP models trained with and without PIWSL

evidence.text: To further assess PIWSL’s impact, we evaluate the robustness during MD simulations of the MLIP models trained with and without PIWSL. We consider MD simulations of the aspirin molecule, with corresponding results presented in figure 3.

evidence.text: In this section, we present a case study demonstrating the application of PIWSL to the fine-tuning of foundation models using a sparse data set.
